en.html:
After some hesitation, I decided to go in human form.

For concealment, the spider shape was better. But even that could not completely deceive an armored warrior's senses. Found out like that, in the present situation, I might be shot down without the courtesy of a single question.

An armored steel spider saying, 'Civilian, I am civilian'—who was going to listen?

迷ったが、結局は人型で行動することに決めた。

　蜘蛛の姿の方が隠形術には優れる。
　しかし武者の感覚まで騙し切れるものではないし、
そうして発見された場合、今の情勢下では問答無用で
撃墜されてしまいかねない。

　甲鉄造りの蜘蛛が自分は民間人だと言い張っても、
耳を貸す者はいないだろう。

en.html:
He should have returned to Fudaraku Castle.

Apparently something was changing the whole situation around Kamakura. Or Kanto? The whole of Yamato? How far this trouble extended, I did not know.
The shogunate troops surrounding Kenchouji had withdrawn like the tide. They had not even spared the time to arrest the people inside the temple.

Saved, yes. In that sense, we were saved.

...In my own case, nothing at all was settled.

I had to follow Kageaki.
Follow him—and do what I must, as his tsurugi.

ja.html:
普陀楽の城へ戻ったはずだった。

　何やらこの鎌倉を――この関東を？　この大和を？
――包む状況が劇的な変化に晒されているらしい。
　建朝寺を囲んだ幕府の一団は、潮が引くように去り、
去るに際して寺の面々を捕らえる手間さえ惜しんだ。

　助かったといえば、助かったのだが。

　……私としては何も解決していない。

　景明を追わなくてはならなかった。
　追い――彼の劒冑として、すべきことをせねばなら
ない。

en.html:
I kept off the main streets, moving from one narrow alley into the next.

The foreigners now filling Kamakura—neither Yamato people nor Emishi, this occupation army—wanted everyone inside their houses. Stay inside, stay inside. Such concern for my whereabouts. Unfortunately my master was not inside the nearest house, so the instruction was not helping.

Being found would lead to nothing pleasant. In this Emishi form, perhaps they would not attack immediately. But wave me through? Haan, certainly. One strange woman running through a military operation, obviously she must have important personal business. Let her go wherever she likes.

No. They would almost certainly detain me.

And I could not afford detention. Already I had been locked up once; no need to tour the enemy's facilities for comparison. Wait for a chance to slip away? This was a proper army, not a roomful of people who might become distracted if I pointed behind them. Escaping would be far too dangerous.

Better not to be found at all. No encounter, no explanation, no need to discover how much understanding could be squeezed out of a soldier with orders.

ja.html:
大通りを避け、路地の狭間から狭間へ移る。

　今、鎌倉を埋め尽くしつつある集団――進駐軍とか
呼ばれている、大和人ではなく蝦夷でもない異国人の
軍勢――は、どうやら民衆を家に閉じ込めておきたい
らしい。繰り返される放送がそう告げている。

　見つかると、面白くないことになりそうだった。
　この蝦夷の姿ならいきなり攻撃されることもないだ
ろうが、さりとて見逃してもらえるとも思えない。

　拘束されるのは避けられまいし、そうなっては困る。
　隙を見て抜け出すにしても、歴とした軍隊が相手で
は余りに危険が大き過ぎる。

　細心の注意を払って見つからないよう心掛けるに、
<ruby>如<rt>し</rt></ruby>くはなかった。

en.html:
A river, not especially wide, ran beside the road. I checked it against the map in my head. I had run through this town enough times; getting properly lost would take some effort.

A tributary of the Kashio River, which ran around the outside of Fudaraku Castle.
If this river was here... the castle was close now.

I drove my legs harder and ran.

道路の傍らにさほど広くもない川が流れているのを
見て、脳裏の地図と突き合わせる。
　この町中は幾度も駆け巡ったから、そう迷うことも
なかった。

　普陀楽城の外周を覆う、<ruby>柏尾川<rt>かしおがわ</rt></ruby>の支流だ。
　ここにこれがあるということは……もう近い。

　足に鞭を入れて、走る。

en.html:
Then I stopped, unable to move.

Fudaraku Castle—
Right in front of me. I could see it. Almost under my nose.

In physical distance, so little remained.

But physical distance was not the whole matter.
In reality, it might as well have been endlessly far away.

en.html:
Rows of infantry, guns ready.
Cannon with their mouths all facing the same way, spitting fire.
Iron vehicles waiting for their moment to charge.

From the castle walls, gunfire and shellfire came back at them.
Above the drifting smoke, armored warriors on both sides moved freely through the sky. Clash, separate. Separate, clash again.

The sounds and flashes of steel and fire scattered and vanished. Lives went into that dazzling whirl one after another. One life finished, then the next. No pause between.
Already the Kashio River was taking red into its surface.

ja.html:
銃を構えた歩兵の隊列。
　筒先を揃えて火を吹く砲門群。
　突進の機を待ち構える鉄の車両。

　それらに向けて放たれる、城壁からの射撃、砲撃。
　噴煙たなびく先の空を見れば、両陣の武者が自在に
舞い、剣を交えては打ち離れ、離れてはまた打ち交え。

　鉄火の響きと輝きを儚く散らし、命を一つまた一つ
と、その繚乱の渦へ沈めてゆく。
　柏尾川の<ruby>面<rt>おも</rt></ruby>は早くも、<ruby>朱<rt>あけ</rt></ruby>の<ruby>彩<rt>いろ</rt></ruby>を加えられつつあった。

en.html:
It had begun.

The vast foreign army on one side.
On the other, the Rokuhara shogunate's forces—with Kageaki among them.

The war between them.
—Already begun. Whatever I still had to do, it had not waited for me.
